videos.script: The office has bought a new computer for the reception desk. It arrives with Windows already on it, and Ana's first task is to decide whether that copy of Windows stays. {{arrives}} Computers from a shop come with extra programs, trial antivirus and the maker's utilities. Many support teams wipe that and install Windows cleanly, so every office machine starts the same way. {{clean}} Installing Windows is mostly waiting. The parts that are not waiting are a handful of decisions, and two of them are expensive to undo. {{decisions}} Which disk, and what happens to what is already on it. And which account the computer is set up with, because that decides who owns it, where its encryption key is kept, and how it is managed later. {{two}} You will check whether a computer can run Windows 11, make an installation USB stick and start the computer from it. You will understand the partitions Windows creates, and get through the first-start screens with the right answers. Then you will do the six things every new installation needs before anybody uses it. {{steps}} And you will learn the difference between upgrading, resetting and installing from scratch, so you can choose the lightest one that fixes the problem in front of you. {{title}}
